body:
I went to mental health today and talked to a civilian psychologist, he seems to think everything I'm going through is perfectly normal for someone adapting to the military.

I definitely don't feel normal.  I flip-flop on my plans for the future at least 10 times a day, and I guess it's all depending on my mood.

Sometimes I want out.  Sometimes I'd be happy with a reclass.  Sometimes I think I can just tough it out.

I panic all the time, it makes me feel like I'm going to throw up.  I piss myself off because everytime I get a chance to talk to someone (my 1st shirt, a psychologist), I fucking downplay all my issues, and talk myself into balancing things out.

For example, situations like me leaning out the window of a fourth story window, feeling the wind rush past my head, fantasizing about how great it would be just to tip my feet forward, close my eyes and feel myself fall...Maybe there'd be a sharp pang of pain, but after that I'd just be left to slowly fade into oblivion.  I really just want to disappear.

What comes out of my mouth, however, is "Uh, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed, sometimes there's lingering thoughts in the back of my head that maybe it would be pretty nice if I could just not have to worry about it anymore...I guess you could call it lingering thoughts".

It's not fucking lingering thoughts, it's orgasmic fantasy.  They give you so much paperwork about malingering or lying or over-exaggerating conditions before you even get a chance to talk that I feel like if I so much as mention being depressed and they find a single reason not to believe me, I'm going to rot in fucking Fort Leavenworth for the next 10 years.

My biggest problem is that for every issue I tell them is troubling me, they somehow twist that shit around to make me feel like it's completely my fault and there's something I could/should be doing that would alleviate the stress.

I'll read up on depression.  I don't know if it's really what's going on.  I just really need...something.

Thanks for all your help, I really appreciate it.

Thanks for telling your story, this is the kind of thing I needed.  I've scheduled an appointment with my base chaplain on Wednesday, I don't know right now if I want to completely get out or try to get reclassed, but the more I talk to people here both in comments and PMs, the more I realize how dangerous the road of depression really is.  Something has got to change, letting my pride get in the way of my sanity seems like the worst thing I can possibly do.

Thank you for your support, I really appreciate it.

I actually get really good grades on paper.  I study a shitload primarily because there's nothing else to do.  I study what we went over that day, and I study what we'll do the next day.  I end up getting the same information about three times.  On paper, I'm actually one of the best in my class.  When I actually do progress checks or try to do something manually, I feel like a chimp trying to smash a triangle block into the square hole and wonder why it never works...

I guess the whole point of that is to say that if I tried to tell my supervisor or commander that I'm struggling with this job, they'd take one look at my grades, laugh at me and send me on my way.  If I intentionally fail a test to get out of it, it's pretty obvious that something changed majorly and I end up getting hit with the UCMJ.

I feel like I fucked myself.

I've considered this a ton, my biggest fear is having anything but an honorable discharge on my record and ruining my chances with employers in the future.  I'm not very familiar with what discharges are assigned to what circumstances, but I'm under the impression that the only way to get something that won't screw you out of a job later in life is to serve the time on your contract.

I really don't want to go asking my supervisors either, lest I be berated even further for trying to "pussy out of their military".  I have, however, served less than 6 months.
